summary.text: Eric Conroy, a Republican, Cincinnati native and U.S. Air Force Academy graduate who served in the Air Force and later worked as a CIA case officer, lost the November 3, 2026 election for U.S. House in Ohio's 1st Congressional District to Greg Landsman.
He announced his candidacy in July 2025 and said he was running on national security, border security, fiscal responsibility and energy independence.

paragraphs.text: Conroy was born and raised on the West Side of Cincinnati and graduated from Elder High School.
He graduated from the U.S. Air Force Academy in 2011 and served in the Air Force until 2018.
He later worked overseas in national security as a CIA case officer, according to his campaign materials, and Fox News described him as a former CIA case officer when he announced his campaign.
WCPO reports that he was stationed in Afghanistan, Poland and Iraq before moving back to Cincinnati.
Conroy earned a graduate degree from Columbia University in 2025.
He announced his campaign for Ohio's 1st District in July 2025, and his Ballotpedia survey says he has been endorsed by U.S. Sen. Bernie Moreno.
WCPO reported that he won the Republican primary in May 2026, describing him as Trump-backed, and that he would face Democratic Rep. Greg Landsman in the November general election.
He received 42.9% of the vote to Greg Landsman's 54.4%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.

sources.title: SCOOP: Former CIA officer, Air Force veteran launches GOP campaign for Dem-held Ohio district
Trump-backed Eric Conroy wins Republican primary for Ohio's 1st Congressional District
